content.text:
Everything is built, typechecked, linted, and smoke-tested end-to-end. Here's a summary of what I implemented.

## What I built

**Auth.js (NextAuth v5)** with two providers, JWT sessions, backed entirely by `src/lib/users.ts`:

- **Email/password** — Credentials provider. `authorize` calls `verifyCredentials()` in `users.ts`, which checks a bcrypt hash.
- **Google sign-in** — OAuth provider. On first sign-in, the `signIn` callback provisions a user record via `findOrCreateOAuthUser()` so Google users land in the same store as everyone else.
- **`/dashboard` protection** — an edge `proxy.ts` (Next 16 renamed `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts`; I ran the migration) redirects unauthenticated requests to `/login?callbackUrl=...`. The dashboard page also re-checks server-side as defense in depth.

**`src/lib/users.ts`** changes: added `passwordHash?` to `User`, plus `getUserByEmail`, `verifyCredentials`, `createUserWithPassword`, `findOrCreateOAuthUser`. `getCurrentUser()` now reads the real session instead of hardcoding `users[0]`. The two seed users (Ada, Grace) got a demo password — `password123` — so they still work as logins.

**New pages**: `/login` (server component, toggles sign-in/sign-up via `?mode=signup`, plus a Google button) backed by Server Actions in `login/actions.ts`. Dashboard got a working sign-out button.

**Architecture note**: split `auth.config.ts` (edge-safe: callbacks only) from `auth.ts` (full config with providers) since Credentials/bcrypt can't run in the Edge runtime used by `proxy.ts` — this is Auth.js's documented pattern for Next.js middleware.

**Verified live** (not just build-clean): unauthenticated `/dashboard` → 307 redirect to `/login`; sign-in with seeded credentials → session cookie → dashboard shows correct user; wrong password → rejected; sign-up form → creates user, auto-signs-in, new user appears in the team list; duplicate email on sign-up → rejected with an error message.

**Credentials**: `.env.example` has placeholders for `AUTH_SECRET`, `AUTH_GOOGLE_ID`, `AUTH_GOOGLE_SECRET` (real Google OAuth credentials needed for Google sign-in to work — email/password works out of the box once `AUTH_SECRET` is set).

One thing worth flagging: since `src/lib/users.ts` is an in-memory array, all accounts (including sign-ups) reset on server restart — that was already true of the existing user store, so I kept it rather than introducing a database as a scope decision you didn't ask for.
